title: To Critic Or Not To Critic
abstract: arXiv:2611.32013v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As large language models tackle longer and more complex tasks, understanding when a critic improves the efficiency of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes increasingly important. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) trains a critic to reduce variance and provide fine-grained credit assignment, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) drops the critic and avoids the bias of bootstrapping from the critic's value estimates. Although recent critic-based methods have reported strong performance relative to GRPO, it remains unclear when each approach is preferable. We argue that there is no universal answer; instead, the choice depends on several interacting factors, including batch size, critic reliance, and task complexity. We study the bias-variance tradeoff in terms of gradient direction, measuring how closely each method's gradient estimates align with the true policy gradient as batch size grows. translated_title: 用还是不用评论家：这是个问题
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型处理越来越长、越来越复杂的任务，理解评论家网络何时能提升强化学习（RL）的效率变得日益重要。近端策略优化（PPO）通过训练评论家网络来降低方差并提供细粒度的信用分配，而组相对策略优化（GRPO）则舍弃评论家网络，从而避免了基于评论家价值估计进行自举所带来的偏差。尽管近期基于评论家的方法相对于GRPO报告了出色的性能，但何时选择哪种方法仍不明确。我们认为这个问题没有普适的答案；相反，方法的选择取决于多个相互作用的因素，包括批次大小、对评论家的依赖程度以及任务复杂度。我们从梯度方向的角度研究偏差-方差的权衡，衡量随着批次大小的增加，每种方法的梯度估计与真实策略梯度的契合程度。在共享的演员目标函数下，我们……
tldr: 本文从梯度方向的偏差-方差权衡入手，揭示PPO（带评论家）与GRPO（不带评论家）之间没有普适的优劣答案，方法选择取决于批次大小、对评论家的依赖程度和任务复杂度等相互作用因素。
en_tdlr: There is no universal answer to whether to use a critic in RL for LLMs; the choice between PPO and GRPO depends on interacting factors such as batch size, critic reliance, and task complexity, analyzed through the bias-variance tradeoff in gradient direction.
